Header: Mikania micrantha Mile-a-minute weed, American rope, Chinese creeper, climbing hempweed, Mikania vine

Prevention: Avoid heavy grazing and browsing since the weed thrives in open, disturbed areas.
As seeds can travel on animals and machinery, do not allow animals into an affected area, limit machinery use in the area and keep machinery clean to prevent spread.
Monitoring: Vigorous, fast-growing, perennial, creeping or twining plant.
Flowers: arranged in large, loose heads; white or cream; produce many seeds.
Stems: herbaceous to semi-woody; ribbed; slighty hairy.
Leaves: smooth; triangular; toothed; 6-15 cm long, 3-9 cm wide.
Look along waterways and transport routes.
Seeds disperse via water, wind animals and vehicles.

Direct Control: For rubber plantations: graze fields with sheep – they will eat the weed first and leguminous ground cover last.
Allow a herb layer to establish in managed orchards, forests or perennial crop fields (such as tea) in order to shade out weed.
Cut near ground once a month for three consecutive months in summer and autumn, and then in winter and spring – this can eliminate 90% of weed.
Hand-pull prior to seed maturity or during the rainy season.
Sickle weed before seed sets – this gives temporary control.
Weed regrows quickly from cut stumps.
Do not leave weed fragments on the ground – they can take root and establish as new plants.
If available in your country, use the biocontrol agent, Puccinia spegazzinii , a rust to control the weed.
